rationale:
## Diagnosis
The primary bottleneck is the solver's heuristic strategy (brute-force permutations only for n <= 9, identity sequence otherwise) which produces trivial/bad sequences on all instances with n >= 10 (evident in score spread: tai20_20.txt scores ~0.67-0.69, tai100_10.txt ~0.72-0.80, tai200_10.txt ~0.81-0.87). This caps the mean at 0.795 despite 0.205 headroom, as better constructive heuristics (NEH-style) reliably reach 0.85+. The pre-existing makespan helper and index guards were not leveraged for a scalable approach, and the permutation branch remains a failure mode on >75% of tested instances.

## Intervention
Replace strategy with neh_heuristic solver_lib helper (O(n^2 m) effective with maintained C updates, fully using injected makespan, handles n/m=0 gracefully, returns 0-based sequence): pre_process sets additional_context to force solver to invoke it unconditionally for flow_shop_scheduling (bypassing permutations/trivial entirely). Targets only this task; generalizes via size/metadata checks.

## Why this is different
Unlike prior layer's incremental makespan patches + partial NEH guidance (which left the solver still defaulting to permutations), we eliminate the failing branch with a drop-in, self-contained library function the solver calls directly rather than attempting to patch its own incomplete logic.
